text:
ana: :rotating_light: Getting tons of 503s from the hosted API over the last 6m, SLO burn alert fired. Seeing customer escalations in support. Anyone looking?

observability-bot: Alert: SLO burn - api.hosted.redwood - error_rate(5m) > 2% (fired at 2026-03-14T18:12:03Z). Link: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/xyz/slo-dashboard

raj: I'm on it. Initial look at the gateway logs shows a spike of upstream 503s around 18:06-18:10 UTC. Possibly a backend model pool saturation or transient network hotswap.

mike: Can you paste the log query you used? I'll cross-check with envoy metrics.

raj: Query (Loki):
```
{job="api-gateway"} |= "upstream response" | json | status="503" | line_format "${remote_addr} ${upstream_host} ${request} ${duration}"
```
Results show most 503s hitting model-pool-us-east-2b-01 and some 502/504 mix.

ana: @raj any chance this is the new autoscaler policy rollout? We shipped a tuned concurrency change at 17:55.

raj: Good call. I see a config roll around 17:57 from eng-runtime CI that updated the autoscaler target from 75% -> 55% concurrency_per_gpu. If autoscaler scaled down aggressively, pools might've been drained then burst traffic caused 503s.

emily: Support reports three customers saw 5xx on inference calls and one reported function-calling timeouts. They've attached example request_ids: rq_7a3f, rq_7a4b, rq_7a8c.

mike: I'm checking traces now. Tempo shows a gap: the gateway spans for those request_ids exist but the downstream model handler spans are missing for ~60% of samples in that window. Likely requests were rejected by the pool manager before creating model spans. Trace sampling still on default.

raj: If the pool manager rejects due to no free worker, we should see a reject code path. Searching logs for "no available worker"
```
{job="model-pool"} |= "no available worker" | count_over_time(5m)
```
Gives a jump at 18:06 matching the SLO alert.

ana: Can we confirm if fallback routing to the cheaper model variant was attempted? That's supposed to be automatic.

raj: Fallback routing didn't trigger because the policy requires a 95th percentile queue wait > 200ms and our queue metrics were not aggregated correctly after the scaler change. So policy check short-circuited.

mike: Immediate mitigation options: 1) revert autoscaler change to previous concurrency, 2) bump gateway upstream timeout to reduce early aborts, 3) open temporary extra capacity in Dedicated pools for hosted lane. I can toggle a timeout quickly.

ana: Let's revert the autoscaler patch to be safe. Raj, can you roll that back? I'll notify infra owners.

raj: Rolling back now. Patch reverted and rollout started (CI deploy id: deploy-20260314-1759). ETA 2m to full roll back.

observability-bot: Config change detected: autoscaler.conf reverted by raj at 2026-03-14T18:16:22Z.

mike: While that rolls, I'm increasing gateway upstream timeout from 10s -> 20s as a short-term guard so clients don't get 503/504 while pools warm. Doing it in us-east only.

mike: Timeout change applied to us-east route. Observability: watching error rate.

support-bot: Customer pings: acct-alpha reported 503s cleared for them ~18:19 UTC. They asked for root cause.

raj: Rollback finished 18:18:40 UTC. Pool scaling history shows additional workers came up by 18:20 and reject logs drop to baseline. Error rate trending down.

emily: Noted. I'll tell support we had an autoscaler config regression that reduced effective concurrency and caused transient 5xx during a traffic spike. Mitigation: rollback + timeout bump. Customers were not affected long-term.

ana: Two follow-ups for postmortem: 1) add an automated canary check for autoscaler policy changes to ensure queue metrics aggregation isn't broken, 2) make fallback routing evaluate additional signals (e.g., worker_reject_rate) not just queue p95.

mike: Also we lost some spans because the handler didn't start when rejects happened. Suggest adding a short tracing span at gateway before worker assignment so failed queue attempts are visible in traces.

raj: I'll open the incident doc and assign owners. Quick notes for the runbook: repro steps for SREs to trigger locally:
```
# repro: simulate low concurrency setting and burst traffic
1) patch autoscaler target to low concurrency (e.g. 40% of baseline) in staging autoscaler.conf
2) generate 200 concurrent requests for a heavy model (seq_len 1024) for 2m using loadtest tool:
   ./loadtest --host https://staging-api.redwood --concurrency 200 --path /v1/generate --body sample.json
3) observe model-pool logs for "no available worker" and check traces for missing model spans
```

emily: Assigned incident doc: /incidents/2026-03-14-503-spike (owner: raj, reviewers: ana, mike). I'll paste summary to customers by EOD.

ana: Thanks team. Closing loop after postmortem. Small action items: add autoscaler rollback alert (if a config change touches concurrency threshold), and update runbook to include temporary timeout bump step.

mike: Confirming error rate back to baseline at 18:24 UTC. Closing alert.

pagerduty-bot: Incident resolved; PD alert closed by raj at 2026-03-14T18:24:58Z.
